title: Combine Two Tables
problemStatement: Report the first name, last name, city and state of each person in the Person table. If the address of a personId is not present in the Address table, report null for city and state.

title: Duplicate Emails
problemStatement: Given a Person table, report all email addresses that occur more than once. Each email contains only lowercase letters and the result may be returned in any order.

title: Customers Who Never Order
problemStatement: Given a Customers table and an Orders table, find all customers who never placed any order. Return the customer names in a column called Customers, in any order.

title: Rising Temperature
problemStatement: Given a Weather table, find all dates' ids with a temperature higher than the temperature of the immediately previous calendar date. Return the result in any order.

title: Weather Observation Station 4
problemStatement: Find the difference between the total number of CITY entries in the STATION table and the number of distinct CITY entries.

title: Second Highest Salary
problemStatement: Given an Employee table, report the second highest distinct salary in a column named SecondHighestSalary. If there is no second highest salary, report null.

title: Department Highest Salary
problemStatement: Given an Employee table and a Department table, find employees who have the highest salary in each of the departments. Report the department name, employee name and salary, in any order.

title: Rank Scores
problemStatement: Given a Scores table, rank the scores from highest to lowest. Equal scores receive the same rank and the next rank after a tie must be the next consecutive integer with no gaps. Order the result by score in descending order.

title: Consecutive Numbers
problemStatement: Given a Logs table with consecutive and increasing ids, find all numbers that appear at least three times consecutively. Report the distinct numbers in a column named ConsecutiveNums, in any order.

title: Exchange Seats
problemStatement: Given a Seat table with continuous ids, swap the seat id of every two consecutive students. If the number of students is odd, the id of the last student is not swapped. Return the result ordered by id in ascending order.

title: Managers with at Least 5 Direct Reports
problemStatement: Given an Employee table where managerId references the id of that employee's manager, find the names of managers who have at least five direct reports. Return the result in any order.

title: Occupations
problemStatement: Pivot the Occupation column in OCCUPATIONS so that each name is sorted alphabetically and displayed underneath its occupation. The output columns are Doctor, Professor, Singer and Actor; print NULL when an occupation has no more names to display.

title: Trips and Users
problemStatement: The cancellation rate of a day is the number of cancelled requests by unbanned users divided by the total number of requests by unbanned users on that day. Given the Trips and Users tables, report the cancellation rate rounded to two decimal places for each day between 2013-10-01 and 2013-10-03. Both the client and the driver of a trip must be unbanned for it to count.

title: Department Top Three Salaries
problemStatement: A company's executives are interested in high earners: employees who have a salary in the top three unique salaries of their department. Given the Employee and Department tables, report the department name, employee name and salary of all high earners, in any order.

title: Human Traffic of Stadium
problemStatement: Given a Stadium table with continuous, increasing ids, display the records of three or more rows with consecutive ids where the number of people is greater than or equal to 100 for each row. Return the result ordered by visit_date in ascending order.

title: Big Countries
problemStatement: A country is big if it has an area of at least three million square kilometres or a population of at least twenty-five million. Given the World table, report the name, population and area of every big country, in any order.

title: Classes More Than 5 Students
problemStatement: Given the Courses table, find all classes that have at least five students. Return the result in any order.

title: Employees With Missing Information
problemStatement: An employee record is incomplete when the employee's name or the employee's salary is missing. Given the Employees and Salaries tables, report the ids of all employees with missing information, ordered by employee_id ascending.

title: Market Analysis I
problemStatement: Given the Users, Orders and Items tables, report for every user their join date and the number of orders they placed as a buyer in 2019. Users with no orders in 2019 must appear with a count of 0. Return the result in any order.

title: Game Play Analysis IV
problemStatement: Given the Activity table, report the fraction of players that logged in again on the day immediately after their first login, rounded to two decimal places.

title: Queries Quality and Percentage
problemStatement: The quality of a query is the average of the ratio rating divided by position, and a query is poor when its rating is below three. Given the Queries table, report for each query name its quality and the percentage of poor queries, both rounded to two decimal places, in any order.

title: Weather Observation Station 20
problemStatement: Given the STATION table, report the median of the LAT_N column rounded to four decimal places.

title: Interviews
problemStatement: Given the Contests, Colleges, Challenges, View_Stats and Submission_Stats tables, report the total number of submissions, accepted submissions, views and unique views for each contest hosted by a hacker. Contests whose four totals are all zero must be excluded. Order the result by contest_id.

title: Not Boring Movies
problemStatement: Given a Cinema table, report the movies with an odd-numbered id whose description is not 'boring'. Return the result ordered by rating in descending order.

title: Employees Earning More Than Their Managers
problemStatement: Given an Employee table with columns id, name, salary and managerId (nullable), find the names of employees who earn more than their direct manager. Return the result in any order.

title: Customer Placing the Largest Number of Orders
problemStatement: Given an Orders table with columns order_number and customer_number, find the customer_number of the customer who placed the largest number of orders. The test data guarantees exactly one customer has the most orders.

title: Actors and Directors Who Cooperated At Least Three Times
problemStatement: Given an ActorDirector table with columns actor_id, director_id and a unique timestamp, find every actor-director pair who have cooperated together at least three times. Return the result in any order.

title: Find Total Time Spent by Each Employee
problemStatement: Given an Employees table with columns emp_id, event_day, in_time and out_time, calculate the total time in minutes spent by each employee on each day. Return the result in any order.

title: Immediate Food Delivery II
problemStatement: A delivery is immediate if the order date equals the customer's preferred delivery date. Given a Delivery table with columns delivery_id, customer_id, order_date and customer_pref_delivery_date, find the percentage of immediate deliveries among each customer's very first order, rounded to two decimal places.

title: Students and Examinations
problemStatement: Given a Students table, a Subjects table and an Examinations table recording one row per exam attempt, report for every student and every subject the number of times that student attended that subject's exam, including zero. Order the result by student_id then subject_name.

title: Product Price at a Given Date
problemStatement: Given a Products table recording every price change of a product on a given change_date, report the price of every product as of 2019-08-16. A product's price is its most recent change on or before that date, or 10 if it has no change on or before that date.

title: Percentage of Users Attended a Contest
problemStatement: Given a Users table and a Register table recording which users registered for which contests, report for every contest the percentage of all users who registered for it, rounded to two decimal places. Order the result by percentage in descending order, breaking ties by contest_id in ascending order.

title: Investments in 2016
problemStatement: Given an Insurance table with columns pid, tiv_2015, tiv_2016, lat and lon, report the sum of tiv_2016 for all policyholders who had the same tiv_2015 value as at least one other policyholder, and who are not located in the same city (the same latitude and longitude) as any other policyholder. Round the result to two decimal places.

title: Average Selling Price
problemStatement: Given a Prices table recording the price of each product over a date range, and a UnitsSold table recording units sold on a purchase date, find the average selling price for each product, rounded to two decimal places. A product with no recorded sales has an average selling price of 0.

title: Reformat Department Table
problemStatement: Given a Department table with columns id, revenue and month (one of 'Jan'..'Dec'), where (id, month) is unique, pivot it into one row per id with a column for each month's revenue (null where no row exists for that month).

title: User Activity for the Past 30 Days I
problemStatement: Given an Activity table recording user actions with possible duplicate rows, report the daily active user count (distinct user_id) for each day between 2019-06-28 and 2019-07-27 inclusive that has at least one recorded activity.

title: Rearrange Products Table
problemStatement: Given a Products table with columns product_id, store1, store2 and store3 (nullable prices), reshape it into rows of (product_id, store, price), one row per product per store that actually has a price. Return the result in any order.

title: Find Followers Count
problemStatement: Given a Followers table with columns user_id and follower_id, report the number of followers for each user. Return the result ordered by user_id ascending.

title: Article Views I
problemStatement: Given a Views table recording each view of an article with columns article_id, author_id, viewer_id and view_date, find all the authors that viewed at least one of their own articles. Return the result sorted by id ascending.

title: Project Employees I
problemStatement: Given a Project table and an Employee table (with experience_years), report the average experience years of all employees for each project, rounded to two decimal places.

title: Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make Any Transactions
problemStatement: Given a Visits table and a Transactions table, find the number of visits that did not result in any transaction, for every customer who has at least one such visit. Return the result in any order.

title: Find Users With Valid E-Mails
problemStatement: Given a Users table with columns user_id, name and mail, find users with a valid email: the local part must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits, underscore, period or dash, followed by exactly '@leetcode.com'. Return the result in any order.

title: Top Travellers
problemStatement: Given a Users table and a Rides table recording the distance travelled on each ride, report the name and total distance travelled by every user, including users with no rides (reported as 0). Order the result by travelled_distance descending, breaking ties by name ascending.

title: Sales Analysis III
problemStatement: Given a Product table and a Sales table (which may contain duplicate rows), report the products that were sold exclusively in the first quarter of 2019 (2019-01-01 through 2019-03-31) and never sold outside that window.

title: Delete Duplicate Emails
problemStatement: Given a Person table with columns id and email, delete all duplicate rows so that only the row with the smallest id is kept for each email. The final Person table should be reported ordered by id.

execution.verificationQuery: SELECT id AS id, email AS email FROM Person ORDER BY id

title: Swap Salary
problemStatement: Given a Salary table with columns id, name, sex ('m' or 'f') and salary, swap every 'm' value to 'f' and every 'f' value to 'm' in the sex column using a single UPDATE statement, without using an intermediate temporary table. Report the final table ordered by id.

execution.verificationQuery: SELECT id AS id, name AS name, sex AS sex, salary AS salary FROM Salary ORDER BY id
